script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Wednesday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed down zero point eight six percent on the session. A mixed day with clear winners and some significant losers pulling weight.

SpaceX reported earnings, and Elon Musk disclosed that his AI and space company will use Nvidia chips exclusively — abandoning Advanced Micro Devices entirely. Advanced Micro Devices fell seven point zero four percent on the session. That single statement moved markets.

The Nasdaq closed lower on Wednesday as technology and communication services names came under broad selling pressure. The Dow Jones, however, posted gains, lifted largely by Nvidia. No major macroeconomic data prints were released Wednesday, leaving earnings reports and corporate commentary as the primary market drivers.

The central story Wednesday belongs to the fallout from SpaceX's earnings call. Elon Musk announced that SpaceX will exclusively use Nvidia chips for its artificial intelligence infrastructure, a direct and public repudiation of Advanced Micro Devices as a supplier. Advanced Micro Devices closed down seven point zero four percent on the session. Micron Technology initially rose on news from the same call — Musk flagged surging memory prices, which was read as a positive demand signal — before retreating to close nearly flat, finishing up just zero point zero six percent. Sandisk, a secondary holding, dropped five point four zero percent after its own earnings release. The through-line here: Nvidia remains the dominant AI chip beneficiary, while competitors and adjacent suppliers saw their narratives punished in real time. Nvidia closed up three point four three percent, reinforcing that gap.

Nvidia was up three point four three percent on the session. That gain came directly from Musk's endorsement of Nvidia as SpaceX's exclusive chip partner. It also absorbed positive downstream commentary from multiple earnings calls across media and real estate sectors that cited Nvidia's infrastructure footprint. Nvidia remains the largest position in this portfolio, and Wednesday's move was a clear net positive contributor.

Turning to Apple, which was up zero point five two percent on the session. A separate report from Yahoo Finance noted that price hikes on consumer electronics may be structural, driven by the AI hardware cycle increasing component costs. Apple, as a premium consumer electronics manufacturer, carries both risk and pricing power in that environment. Watch for any guidance commentary around margin impact.

Over at Alphabet, the session was rough — down four point zero three percent. A headline from finance.yahoo.com framed the stock's calm surface as hiding a turbulent forecast, citing potential valuation swings tied to its legal and AI competitive exposure. Wednesday's move reinforced that concern.

Micron Technology was up zero point zero six percent. As noted in the top story, the initial Musk-driven optimism on memory prices faded. Micron closed nearly flat after a volatile intraday session. Demand signals remain constructive, but execution on the price realization will matter.

Meanwhile, Microsoft was down one point zero nine percent. No specific news drove the move — broader Nasdaq weakness and sector rotation appeared to be the primary factor. Microsoft's next major catalyst remains its cloud and AI infrastructure spending updates.

Amazon was down one point seven two percent. A separate item noted that Amazon's cloud business is growing at a historic pace, but analysts have focused heavily on its data center capital expenditure plans. That spending debate is creating valuation uncertainty in the near term.

Advanced Micro Devices was down seven point zero four percent — the largest single-name loss in the primary portfolio Wednesday. Musk's explicit Nvidia preference on the SpaceX earnings call was a direct competitive blow. Watch for any formal response from Advanced Micro Devices management.

Tesla was down one point seven seven percent. Musk's attention was clearly on SpaceX during Wednesday's cycle. No Tesla-specific catalyst was cited. The stock moved largely in sympathy with broader consumer discretionary weakness and Musk-linked sentiment.

Intel was up zero point two zero percent on the session. A quiet move, and no material news drove it. Intel remains the smallest primary holding by weight, and the marginal gain Wednesday offered little signal in either direction.

Three items to track over the next forty-eight hours. First, watch for any formal response or investor call from Advanced Micro Devices addressing the SpaceX chip news — management commentary could either stabilize or extend Wednesday's selloff. Second, Alphabet faces ongoing scrutiny from analysts following Wednesday's drop, and any developments tied to its legal proceedings or AI competitive positioning should be monitored closely. Third, given the Micron intraday volatility around memory pricing commentary, any follow-up analyst notes or industry data on DRAM and NAND pricing trends in the next day or two will be directly relevant to the memory-heavy exposure in this portfolio.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch whether Advanced Micro Devices stabilizes or continues lower — the answer will say a great deal about how the market is pricing AI chip competition going into the back half of the week.
